 Chhath Puja 2026 school holidays: Will schools remain closed in Delhi, Bihar, UP and West Bengal? Check updates
 Schools in Delhi will remain closed on November 16 for Chhath Puja. Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal may also observe school holidays during the festival period.
 Curated by Yash Wardhan Singh 
 Image: iStock 
 Nov 11, 2026
 Share
 Schools in New Delhi are likely to remain closed on November 16, 2026, due to Chhath Puja. The Delhi Government's General Administration Department shared this information through a post on X (formerly Twitter). 
 According to the official order issued on Monday, November 16 will be observed as a public holiday for Chhath Puja. The holiday is being announced for the final morning rituals of the festival, including Usha Arghya. 
 The order applies to all government offices, autonomous bodies and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) under the Delhi Government. The holiday has been declared for Pratihar Shashthi or Surya Shashthi, also known as Chhath Puja. 
 The official order stated, "The Lieutenant Governor of the National Capital Territory of Delhi is pleased to declare November 16, 2026 (Monday), as a public holiday in all Government Offices, Autonomous Bodies and Public Sector Undertakings under the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, on account of Pratihar Shashthi or Surya Shashthi (Chhath Puja)." 
 The order was issued by Pradeep Tayal, Joint Secretary, General Administration Department (Coordination Branch). 
 Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta had also made a similar announcement last year. 
 Chhath Puja 2026: School holidays in Bihar 
 Chhath Puja is one of the biggest festivals celebrated in Bihar. Schools and colleges across the state are likely to remain closed during the festival. 
 Educational institutions usually get a holiday of three to four days for Chhath Puja. This year, schools may remain closed from November 14 to November 16. 
 Chhath Puja 2026: School holidays in Uttar Pradesh 
 Schools across Uttar Pradesh may also remain closed for Chhath Puja. However, the state government has not yet issued an official notice regarding the holiday. 
 Schools in areas where the festival is celebrated on a large scale, including Varanasi and Gorakhpur, are expected to remain closed. Students and parents are waiting for an official announcement from the state government. 
 Chhath Puja is an important Hindu festival celebrated in honour of the Sun God, Surya, and his wife, Usha, also known as Chhathi Maiya. The festival is mainly observed in Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Nepal's Terai region. Devotees in other parts of India and abroad also celebrate it. 
 Jagadhatri Puja 2026: School holidays in West Bengal 
 Chhath Puja is not widely celebrated across West Bengal. However, the state celebrates Jagadhatri Puja around the same time. 
 The festival is dedicated to Goddess Jagadhatri, who is considered a form of Goddess Durga. She represents strength, protection and patience. 
 Jagadhatri Puja is celebrated on Shukla Navami, the ninth day of the bright half of the Hindu month of Kartik. It usually falls in October or November, around one month after Durga Puja. 
 The celebrations are especially popular in Chandannagar, Krishnanagar and Murshidabad. Schools across West Bengal are likely to remain closed from November 16 to November 20.
